summary: Daniel R. Tuzzeo specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his thesis at Florida State University, where he studied under advisors Jimmy Yu, Bryan J. Cuevas, and Joseph Hellweg.

Daniel Schlumberger (1904–1972) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Strasbourg (~1922–1925), succeeded Joseph Hackin, and held a post at Princeton University (~1967–1972).

Daniel Sperber (born 1940) works in history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at Kol Torah, Kilburn Grammar School, Yeshivah of Flatbush, and University College London (~1965–1968), he held posts at Bar-Ilan University (~1968) and the Open University of Israel.

Daniel Stuart Capper is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar. He earned a BA and MA at the University of Virginia, studying under Robert P. Scharlemann and Jeffrey Hopkins, and completed a PhD at the University of Chicago (attested 2000).

Daniel Timothy Aitken specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Tasmania and studied under Jay L. Garfield, Parimal G. Patil, and Leonard van der Kuijp.

Daniel Veidlinger (born 1970) is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Steven Collins, studied under Samli Mulkæo and Nalini Devdas, and held posts at Chiang Mai University and California State University, Chico.

Daniel W. Kent is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Virginia and served as an instructor at both the University of Virginia and Mary Baldwin University (both attested 2010).
Daniela Berti is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Siena. She held a fellowship at Milieux, Cultures et Sociétés en Himalaya (attested 2004).

Daniela Bevilacqua specializes in Indology and religious studies. She earned PhDs from Sapienza University of Rome and Paris Nanterre University, and later served as a postdoctoral research fellow at SOAS University of London (attested 2020).
Daniele Cuneo held posts at the University of Paris and the Sorbonne (both attested 2018), and later joined the faculty at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2026).
Danielle Feller is an Indologist who completed her PhD at the University of Lausanne in 2001 under doctoral supervisor Johannes Bronkhorst, having also studied under Ganesh U. Thite.
Danping Long is an Indology and Buddhist studies researcher who has pursued doctoral studies at the University of Munich and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (both attested 2026).
Danuta Stasik (born 1956) is an Indologist who studied under Maria Byrski at the University of Warsaw (~1975–1980). She subsequently held academic posts at the University of Warsaw (~1980 and 1986).

Daoquan Yu (1901–1992) was a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Cheeloo University (~1920–1924) and under Jacques Bacot (~1934–1937), later serving as a professor at Minzu University of China (~1953–1992).

Dasharatha Sharma (1903–1976), an Indologist and historian, studied at the University of Delhi. He headed history at Hindu College (~1945–1957) and Jai Narain Vyas University (1966), was Reader at Delhi (~1957–1966), and directed Rajasthan Oriental Research Institute (~1970–1974).

Daud Ali (born 1964) is an Indology and history scholar. He studied at William & Mary and the University of Chicago, taught history at SOAS (~1995–2009), and was appointed associate professor at the University of Pennsylvania in 2009.
David A. Dilworth (born 1934) is a scholar of philosophy and Japanology. He studied under Masao Abe and Valdo H. Viglielmo (1968).

David A. Hall specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Shoshin Ichishima (1976), earned a doctorate from UC Berkeley (by 1990), was a visiting scholar at Taisho University (1977), and chaired a division at Montgomery College (attested 2019).
David Azzopardi specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under doctoral supervisor Kate Crosby (attested 2010).

David B. Gray is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman, held a fellowship at Rice University, and taught at Santa Clara University (attested 2005–2017).
